887.evidence: Another financial crisis for the firm occurred in 1970, when the Penn Central Transportation Company went bankrupt with $87 million in commercial paper outstanding, most of it issued through Goldman Sachs. In 1969, Goldman Sachs allegedly continued to sell the debt to investors despite knowing that Penn Central's financials were deteriorating. In 1970, Goldman Sachs tried to force Penn Central to buy back debt unsold by Goldman Sachs, without extending the same offer to its customers. These actions of alleged impropriety led to an investigation by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission, which was settled. Customers that bought Penn Central debt sued Goldman Sachs; the potential liability could have bankrupted the firm. However, the firm settled the lawsuits, received insurance proceeds, and the value of the debt did recover. The bankruptcy of Penn Central resulted in credit ratings for every issuer of commercial paper today by several credit rating agencies.
